title: Zustand Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Zustand course.

entries.name: Create a small store
entries.summary: A Zustand store groups values and actions.

entries.name: Select one value
entries.summary: A selector chooses the store value a component needs.

example.code:
import {useReading} from "./store.js"; export default function Count(){const count=useReading(state=>state.count);return

Books: {count}

;}

entries.name: Call an action from a button
entries.summary: An action is a function stored alongside the values.

example.code:
import {useReading} from "./store.js";
export default function Add(){const add=useReading(state=>state.add);return <button onClick={add}>Read one</button>;}

entries.name: Base an update on current state
entries.summary: A set callback receives the current state.

entries.name: Update one top-level field
entries.summary: By default, set merges the supplied top-level fields into state.

entries.name: Copy a nested object
entries.summary: A nested object needs its own copy when you change one of its fields.

entries.name: Add an item without changing the old array
entries.summary: A new array can keep the old items and add one more.

entries.name: Calculate a derived count
entries.summary: A selector can calculate a value from stored data.

example.code:
import {useBooks} from "./book-store.js"; export default function Unread(){const count=useBooks(state=>state.books.filter(book=>!book.read).length);return

{count} unread books

;}

entries.name: Use a store without React
entries.summary: A vanilla Zustand store can be used by ordinary JavaScript.

entries.name: Listen and then unsubscribe
entries.summary: subscribe runs a listener after store changes.

entries.name: Save a browser preference
entries.summary: The persist middleware can store selected state in browser storage.

entries.name: Reset only the intended data
entries.summary: A reset action should set the values that belong to its feature.
